summary: Gone: 1934 Civilian Conservation Corps steel lookout in Buncombe County, 45 feet 9 inches tall; the lookout history page lists it as removed, with no date.

facts.design: Steel tower with one-room tower cabin
facts.status_note: Listed as removed with no date; no source describes the site now
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps; 45-foot 9-inch steel tower with a one-room tower cabin for $968.90; Emergency Conservation Works program funding

evidence.supports: built September 1934 by the CCC: 45-foot 9-inch steel tower, one-room tower cabin, $968.90
evidence.quote: September 1934: The Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 45-foot 9-inch steel tower with a 1-room tower cabin for $968.90.
The funding was through the Emergency Conservation Works program.

evidence.supports: details credited to the state's 6th Biennial Report, 1934-36
evidence.quote: (Department of Conservation and Development - 6th Biennial Report 1934-36)

evidence.supports: agency is the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
evidence.quote: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: lookout listed as removed, with no date
state tower index lists High Windy in Buncombe County

corrections.why: Source gives 45 feet 9 inches, about 13.9 m. The brief's 13.7 m is only 45 feet and leaves out the 9 inches.

notes_for_editor: The build details come from one lookout-history page that cites a state biennial report; the removal is listed with no date. Two searches (a Buncombe County fire tower query and a CCC 1934 removal query) found no other description of the tower or its site. No staffing or fire history is in the sources.
